nextGame.blurb: No. 1 Ohio State heads to Austin as a 1.5-point underdog to No. 4 Texas, with ESPN's model giving the Longhorns a 59.7% edge in a game that projects tight on both sides of a 49.5 total. Two of the sport's heavyweights meeting in Week 2 means the loser is instantly playing catch-up in the top-four chase.
No. 6 Oregon travels to Oklahoma State a 23.5-point favorite, and ESPN has the Ducks at 93%. After sliding in the rankings, Oregon could use a statement performance on the road.
No. 2 Georgia hosts Western Kentucky as a 39.5-point favorite and a 99.2% ESPN pick. The Bulldogs lead the SEC picture and have no reason to linger on this one.
No. 3 Notre Dame lays 45.5 against Rice, and ESPN's model gives the Irish a 99.4% chance. Nothing to solve here but the margin.

Two of the sport's heavyweights meeting in Week 2 means the loser is instantly playing catch-up in the top-four chase.
No. 5 Indiana hosts Howard as a 57.5-point favorite with a 66.5 total. The Hoosiers are chasing Ohio State in the Big Ten picture, so the scoreboard is the only thing to watch here.
No. 7 Miami buried Florida A&M 77-7, blowing past even a 59.5-point spread. About as emphatic a tune-up as the Hurricanes could have scripted.
No. 10 Texas A&M lays 14.5 at home to Arizona State, with ESPN giving the Aggies an 88.6% chance. A non-conference test on paper, a get-right spot if A&M plays to the number.
No. 9 Ole Miss is a 45.5-point favorite over Charlotte with a 98.7% win probability from ESPN. A late-afternoon walkover in Oxford unless something strange happens.

No. 11 Oklahoma goes on the road as a 5.5-point favorite at Michigan, and ESPN still likes the Sooners at 64.5%. The 43.5 total says both sides expect this to be decided in the trenches, not in a shootout.
No. 8 LSU is a 35.5-point favorite over Louisiana Tech, with ESPN giving the Tigers a 98.2% chance. A comfortable Saturday night in Baton Rouge on paper.

No. 13 Texas Tech is a 25.5-point favorite at Oregon State, with ESPN giving the Red Raiders a 94% shot. As the current Big 12 pacesetter, Tech's job is simply to avoid the kind of West Coast trip that gets weird.

No. 12 Alabama is a 10-point favorite in Lexington, and ESPN puts the Tide at an 84.6% chance to handle Kentucky. With a 48.5 total, this shapes up as a game Alabama needs to win cleanly rather than survive.

bubbleNote.blurb: Alabama holds the No. 13 seed after moving up a spot, leaving the Tide just one place outside the field. The margin is as thin as it gets on the bubble.

predictions.blurb: Houston nudged up to No. 22 this week, though the advanced numbers remain skeptical with SP+ at 46 and FPI at 41. The resume is outrunning the metrics so far.
SMU climbed two spots to No. 17, and FPI's No. 20 ranking is roughly in line with where the voters have the Mustangs. SP+ at 31 is the lone holdout.
Washington slid from 17th to 19th, with SP+ (29) and FPI (30) both pegging the Huskies right around that neighborhood. The models and the poll are in rare agreement.
Penn State moved up to No. 16, and the metrics love the Nittany Lions more than the poll does — 13th in SP+ and 14th in FPI. That's a team the numbers think is being undersold.
Oregon tumbled from No. 2 to No. 6, but SP+ (7) and FPI (8) still have the Ducks comfortably inside the top 10. The poll may have overcorrected.

fieldStorylines.blurb: No. 1 Ohio State at No. 4 Texas is a bye-line game in September: both are sitting in the band that earns a first-round pass, and the loser takes a real dent in that standing. There aren't many Week 2 games with this much seeding weight attached.
The SEC's automatic bid is a two-team conversation right now, with No. 2 Georgia holding the lead and No. 4 Texas just two spots back. That's close enough that one result flips the order.
No. 13 Texas Tech leads the Big 12 race with No. 15 BYU right on its heels, only two spots separating them. Neither can afford a stumble with the gap this thin.

No. 1 Ohio State sits atop the Big Ten with No. 5 Indiana four spots back — the widest of the three major-conference leads, but hardly safe. Indiana's path is simple: keep winning and wait for the Buckeyes to slip.
